observations: Line 2 concatenates untrusted user_id directly into the SQL string instead of using the parameter tuple, which is returned empty as ().
The behavior contract states the caller passes the returned SQL and parameter tuple to a DB-API driver using %s placeholders, so the empty tuple supplies no bound values.

For probe p1, query('0 OR 1=1') returns the string 'SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = 0 OR 1=1' with an empty tuple; JSON-encoded as an array this is ["SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = 0 OR 1=1", []] (tuple serializes as an empty JSON array).
The injected predicate OR 1=1 is embedded in the SQL text, so the driver executes it as SQL rather than as a literal value, matching the stated SQL-injection concern.
A normal comparison input such as query('42') returns 'SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = 42' with an empty tuple, showing the same concatenation path with no parameter binding.
No static_findings are supplied, so the concatenation on line 2 is the only observable defect in the provided source.
